facts.fact_text: The youth group Committee for Protection of Rights of Young Political Prisoners (Gənc Siyasi Məhbusların Hüquqlarını Müdafiə Komitəsi) decided to hold a demonstration at around 5.30 p.m. on 22 May 2011 at the Seaside Boulevard in Baku.
According to the applicants, the demonstration on 22 May 2011 was intended to be peaceful.
According to the applicants, the demonstration on 22 May 2011 was conducted in a peaceful manner.
The participants of the demonstration on 22 May 2011 were a group of ten to twelve persons.
The participants of the demonstration on 22 May 2011 were demanding the release of young persons arrested during some previous demonstrations.
The applicants attended the demonstration on 22 May 2011 at the Seaside Boulevard in Baku.
Shortly after the demonstration on 22 May 2011 had begun, the police started to disperse it.
According to the applicants, police officers followed and caught the applicants after they attempted to run away from the demonstration.
All three applicants were arrested by police officers V.I. and R.G. at around 5.30 p.m. on 22 May 2011.

Article 49 of the 1995 Constitution of Azerbaijan provides that everyone has the right, having notified respective governmental bodies in advance, to assemble with other people peacefully and without arms, to organise meetings, demonstrations, protests and marches, and to stage pickets.

Under Article 5 of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998, advance written notification is required in order to agree upon the place and time of an assembly and upon the route of a march, with the purpose of enabling the relevant local executive authority to take necessary measures.
Under Article 5 of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998, the notification has to be done in writing five days before the demonstration.
Under Article 5 § IV of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998, no prior written notification was required for spontaneous assemblies.

At the material time, Article 14 § I(2) of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that police authorities have the power, when necessary, to stop an assembly which has not been notified to the authorities beforehand, save for spontaneous assemblies.

At the material time, Article 14 § I(4) of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that police authorities have the power to apprehend and remove from the place where an event is being held persons who came carrying weapons, rocks, pieces of wood and glass, clubs that may pose a threat to people's life and safety or damage property, explosives, flammables, or radioactive materials.

At the material time, Article 14 § II(2) of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that police authorities have the power to order the organisers and participants of an assembly to use all available opportunities to stop the assembly and to disperse, in execution of orders specified under Article 8 paragraphs V and VI of that Law.

At the material time, Article 14 § II(3) of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that police authorities have the power to warn organisers and participants that physical force or exceptional measures will be used against them if the order to stop the assembly and to disperse is not complied with.

At the material time, Article 14 § II(4) of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that police authorities have the power to use physical force or exceptional measures in order to stop an assembly and disperse participants, in accordance with the legislation of the Republic of Azerbaijan.

At the material time, Article 14 § II(5) of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that police authorities have the power to apprehend persons not complying with the order to stop an assembly and disperse.

At the material time, Article 14 § VI of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that the use of physical force or exceptional measures by police officers in all circumstances must be proportionate to an existing threat.

At the material time, Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences provided that any breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies, demonstrations, protests, marches and pickets shall be punishable by a reprimand or a fine of seven to thirteen Azerbaijani manats.

At the material time, Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences provided that deliberate failure by an individual to comply with the lawful order of a police officer or military serviceman carrying out their duties to protect public order shall be punishable by a fine of twenty to twenty-five Azerbaijani manats or, if that sanction is inadequate in the circumstances of the case and taking into account the character of the offender, by administrative detention for a term of up to fifteen days.

At the material time, Article 410.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences provided that an individual who is subject to administrative-offence proceedings or a representative of a legal entity shall be given an opportunity to familiarise with the administrative-offence report.

At the material time, Article 410.4 of the Code of Administrative Offences provided that an individual who is subject to administrative-offence proceedings or a representative of a legal entity has the right to a copy of the administrative-offence report.

At the material time, Article 414.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences provided that a report concerning an administrative offence punishable by administrative detention shall be sent to a judge for examination immediately after it has been drawn up.

At the material time, Article 422.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences provided that cases concerning an administrative offence punishable by administrative detention shall be examined on the day of receipt by the court of an administrative-offence report.

At the material time, Article 422.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences provided that cases against persons subjected to administrative arrest shall be examined at the latest within 48 hours of their arrest.

At the material time, Article 14 § I(4) of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that police authorities have the power to apprehend and remove from the place where an event is being held persons who came carrying weapons, rocks, pieces of wood and glass, clubs that may pose a threat to people's life and safety or damage property, explosives, flammables, or radioactive materials.

Shortly after the demonstration on 22 May 2011 had begun, the police started to disperse it.
According to the applicants, as soon as they noticed the police approaching they attempted to run away and leave the place of the demonstration.
According to the applicants, police officers followed and caught the applicants after they attempted to run away from the demonstration.

Police officers V.I. and R.G. submitted a report (raport) to a superior police officer stating that at around 5.30 p.m. at the Seaside Boulevard a group of young persons attempted to hold an unauthorised demonstration by shouting out loud and disturbed people.
Police officers V.I. and R.G. stated in their report that when they wanted to calm down those persons, the persons ignored them.

At the material time, Article 14 § VI of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that the use of physical force or exceptional measures by police officers in all circumstances must be proportionate to an existing threat.

The Report CommDH(2013)14 noted that the most frequent problems encountered included the banning of demonstrations in central and easily accessible locations and the use of force to disperse demonstrations, leading to arrests and in some cases harsh sentences.

The Human Rights Watch Report (2013) stated that the Azerbaijani authorities have broken up unsanctioned demonstrations, often with violence, and have arrested and imprisoned peaceful protestors, organizers, and participants.
The Human Rights Watch Report (2013) stated that for several years police have dispersed, at times violently, peaceful protests in Baku's center.
According to the applicants, they were never served with copies of the administrative-offence reports.
According to the applicants, they were never served with other documents in their case files.
According to the applicants, they were not given access to a lawyer after the arrest or while they were kept in police custody.

According to the first applicant, Mr Agasif Ibrahimov, members of the public, including human rights defenders and journalists, were not allowed to attend the hearing before the Sabail District Court.
The first applicant, Mr Agasif Ibrahimov, was not represented by any lawyer at the hearing before the Sabail District Court.
According to the first applicant, Mr Agasif Ibrahimov, he was not given an opportunity to hire a lawyer of his own choice.
According to the second applicant, Mr Emin Farhadi, members of the public were not allowed to attend the hearing before the Sabail District Court.
According to the second applicant, Mr Emin Farhadi, the Sabail District Court had not taken a formal decision to close the hearing to the public.
The second applicant, Mr Emin Farhadi, was not represented by any lawyer at the hearing before the Sabail District Court.
According to the second applicant, Mr Emin Farhadi, he was not given an opportunity to hire a lawyer of his own choice.

The third applicant, Mr Jamil Hajiyev, was not represented by any lawyer at the hearing before the Sabail District Court.
According to the third applicant, Mr Jamil Hajiyev, he was not given an opportunity to hire a lawyer of his own choice.
The only witness questioned during the court hearing of the third applicant, Mr Jamil Hajiyev, before the Sabail District Court was police officer R.G.
The third applicant, Mr Jamil Hajiyev, complained in his appeal before the Baku Court of Appeal that his arrest had been unlawful.
The third applicant, Mr Jamil Hajiyev, complained in his appeal before the Baku Court of Appeal that the hearing before the Sabail District Court had not been fair.
The third applicant, Mr Jamil Hajiyev, requested the Baku Court of Appeal to quash the Sabail District Court's decision.

The Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, in document CommDH(2011)33 dated 29 September 2011, noted that his attention was drawn to the wave of arrests of activists and political opponents in connection with protests held in Baku in March and April 2011.

According to information received by the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, the protests held in Baku in March and April 2011 were sometimes dispersed with excessive force and the work of journalists was hindered.

The Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe urged the Azerbaijani authorities to ensure that the right to freedom of peaceful assembly is fully guaranteed in Azerbaijan, in accordance with the Court's case-law.

In the Report CommDH(2013)14 dated 6 August 2013, Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe Nils Muižnieks noted that the issue of limitations imposed on freedom of assembly had regularly been raised by local and international observers in recent years.
Commissioner Nils Muižnieks called on the Azerbaijani authorities to adopt effective measures to prevent the use of force against peaceful protestors by law enforcement officials.
Commissioner Nils Muižnieks expressed concern relating to the reported non-implementation of due process standards in proceedings brought against participants in unauthorised demonstrations.

Commissioner Nils Muižnieks stated that participants in peaceful assemblies should not be sanctioned for the mere fact of being present at and actively participating in the demonstration in question, provided they do not do anything illegal, violent or obscene in the course of it.
Commissioner Nils Muižnieks urged the Azerbaijani authorities to ensure that no disproportionate sanction, which would undermine the fundamental right to peaceful assembly, is imposed.
Commissioner Nils Muižnieks called on the Azerbaijani authorities to ensure the full respect of fair trial guarantees for protesters.
